claims.explanation: Navitoclax kills cells by inhibiting the anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family proteins BCL-2 and BCL-XL, so selectivity is expected to track with dependence on these proteins for survival rather than with any single lineage. The strongest predictor is high expression of the drug's targets (BCL2, BCL2L1/BCL-XL, and possibly BCL2L2), which creates an apoptotic block that navitoclax can release; this is supported by the drug's mechanism and by the senolytic literature showing BCL-XL dependence in sensitive cells. Activating CTNNB1 mutations appear enriched among sensitive lines and have been reported to associate with navitoclax sensitivity, while loss of pro-apoptotic effectors such as TP53-pathway or apoptotic priming differences may modulate response.

Intact p53-mediated apoptosis may be needed for efficient navitoclax killing; TP53-mutant lines are enriched among resistant lines
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines appear among sensitive lines and navitoclax restores apoptosis in EGFR inhibitor-resistant cells
BRAF-mutant lines appear among sensitive lines, possibly reflecting MAPK-driven apoptotic priming
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling and is enriched in resistant lines
NF1 loss may increase RAS/MAPK signaling and apoptotic priming in some sensitive lines
ATM loss may impair DNA-damage-induced apoptotic signaling and is seen in resistant lines
KRAS-mutant lines appear among sensitive lines, consistent with oncogene-driven priming
CDKN2A loss may reflect increased proliferative and apoptotic priming in sensitive lines
